work_type: Data availability inventory only; no fit, prediction, selection or performance re-evaluation.

audit_scope.whole_file_metadata_exception: Only headers, row counts, bytes and SHA256 cover complete raw files.

event_clock_contract.equal_timestamp_rule: Event exactly at t is unknown as an input; customer delivery <= t conservatively suppresses checkpoint alerts. Carrier-trigger decision occurs at carrier + 1ns.
event_clock_contract.timezone: Timezone-naive Olist export; geographic timezone/ingestion clocks are not provided.
event_clock_contract.inventory_boundary: 2018-05-01T00:00:00 exclusive for all operational observations and queries.
event_clock_contract.promise_end: Midnight after original estimated delivery calendar date; a future contractual promise can be known before its date, subject to revision availability assumptions.
event_clock_contract.advance_reminder_eligibility: Require no delivery <= t, no observed invalid carrier chronology, known promise and t < promise-end midnight. Already-overdue pending is monitoring rather than prospective delay prediction.
event_clock_contract.ingestion_limitation: Recorded event time is not proof that production systems had ingested that event by the same instant.

shipping_schedule_and_item_granularity.assumption: Exported item dispatch schedule is assumed available at approval only in the existing sensitivity branch; creation/revision/ingestion timestamps are absent.
shipping_schedule_and_item_granularity.proxy_limit: One order-level carrier timestamp cannot establish actual dispatch of every item or seller; carrier-vs-limit is descriptive, not a dispatch-lateness target.

0.eligibility_note: Features observe event < t; delivery <= t and observed invalid carrier chronology suppress generic reminders. The two normal-state partitions sum to generic eligible; invalid-carrier rows are a separate exclusion. Advance reminders additionally require known promise and t < midnight after promised date; already-overdue orders are monitoring, not future-delay classification. Unknown cancellation times remain; this is not the current labeled delivered-only scoring cohort.

handover_history_feasibility.event_definition: Valid approval<=carrier<cutoff, independent of final status; each query uses carrier in [query-90days,query).
handover_history_feasibility.source_assumptions: Export event time stands for timely availability; order-level primary seller chosen by highest item price then lowest item ID; route uses static master states.
handover_history_feasibility.not_measured: Support only; no fitted model, recall estimate, latency feature selection by target, or post-cutoff order outcomes.

profile_period_interpretation.all_pre_cutoff: Coverage of valid approved orders before May1, including unfinished/missing-item orders; no outcome label filter.
profile_period_interpretation.2017-07_and_2017-09: Previously inspected historical-validation approval months; this inventory computes operational counts only.
profile_period_interpretation.2017-12_2018-02_and_2018-04: Previously inspected development approval months; this inventory computes operational counts only.
profile_period_interpretation.right_censoring: Physical events and checkpoint queries are censored at May1; especially April completed-event duration summaries omit handovers not yet observed and do not prove faster service.
profile_period_interpretation.comparability: These all-approved operational populations differ from the existing eventually-delivered eligible prediction cohort; their denominators are not alert-performance denominators.

prediction_time_inventory.known: Purchase/approval clocks, original promise and transaction attributes under static-export availability assumptions; strictly earlier historical carrier/delivery events.
prediction_time_inventory.unknown: This order's future carrier event, actual transit/delivery duration, final status and future reviews.
prediction_time_inventory.new_signal_opportunity: Historical carrier handover speed and approved-but-not-yet-handed-over backlog; preserve the existing approval-time cohort and daily cap.

prediction_time_inventory.known: Recorded order-level carrier event; elapsed approval-to-carrier time and original promise remaining at this later decision.
prediction_time_inventory.unknown: Future customer delivery, actual parcel/item scans, carrier identity, final outcome.
prediction_time_inventory.new_signal_opportunity: Separate later-intervention task; excludes unhanded-over orders and needs a new cohort/budget definition.

prediction_time_inventory.known: Elapsed approval time; only carrier/customer events strictly earlier than checkpoint; original promise remaining.
prediction_time_inventory.unknown: Any later event; why a timestamp is missing; cancellation time; event ingestion delay.
prediction_time_inventory.new_signal_opportunity: Event-observed pending/handed-over state; one decision per order or repeat-alert policy must be defined first.

prediction_time_inventory.known: A valid earlier carrier event, elapsed transit proxy and whether customer delivery was observed before checkpoint.
prediction_time_inventory.unknown: Carrier/parcel scan positions and final delivery outcome.
prediction_time_inventory.new_signal_opportunity: Transit monitoring among handed-over yet unreceived orders; daily eligible-order cap cannot be compared directly with approval-batch 10%.

candidate_signal_inventory.safe_clock: Other orders' valid carrier >= their approval, carrier strictly < current approval; rolling event-time window; no final-status/delivery filter; exclude current order.
examples: seller/global/route handover count and approval-to-carrier hours over trailing 90 days
candidate_signal_inventory.risk: Completed-handover history omits still-unhanded-over orders; seller sparsity and anomalous clocks require missingness/count controls.

candidate_signal_inventory.safe_clock: Other approvals < current approval; carrier missing or >= query; do not read final order_status; invalid carrier chronology must be flagged separately.
candidate_signal_inventory.risk: Missing events and absent cancellation clocks can inflate queue; proxy does not establish physical possession.

candidate_signal_inventory.safe_clock: Use schedule values only if their creation/version is confirmed available at prediction time; never treat shipping_limit_date as actual dispatch.
candidate_signal_inventory.risk: No schedule revision/creation timestamp; already evaluated as a sensitivity branch, not a new uncontaminated signal.

candidate_signal_inventory.safe_clock: Carrier event must already be observed strictly before a later decision; valid carrier >= approval.
examples: promise hours remaining at carrier observation
candidate_signal_inventory.risk: Leaks future at approval; changing to handover time changes population and available intervention lead time.

candidate_signal_inventory.safe_clock: At predeclared checkpoint t, only event timestamps < t are observed; events exactly t remain unknown.
examples: no carrier event observed by approval+3d
carrier observed but no customer delivery observed by approval+7d
candidate_signal_inventory.risk: Requires repeated decision policy and event ingestion audit; final snapshot status is not historical as-of status.

candidate_signal_inventory.safe_clock: Existing physical-delivery history < approval; no future label history; backlog uses approval/promise and observed delivery clocks.
candidate_signal_inventory.risk: Already present; renaming/recombining does not create a new external logistics observation.

candidate_signal_inventory.safe_clock: Requires new timestamped external data and joining/availability rules.
candidate_signal_inventory.risk: Cannot invent these from city/ZIP or a final delivery timestamp; day-of-week already exists.

candidate_signal_inventory.safe_clock: No historical status transition timestamps exist; reviews are downstream outcomes, not approval-time predictors.
examples: actual customer delivery date as own-order input
candidate_signal_inventory.risk: Future information or target leakage; not proposed for the next training change.

limitations: One order-level carrier/customer timestamp does not identify each parcel, carrier, item or seller's movement.
No cancellation/status-transition/scan/ingestion or master-data revision history; missing observations cannot be equated with a verified physical state.
Transaction/product/location/schedule fields come from a final static export; availability and versions at approval are assumptions, not proven ingestion logs.
Event profile counts and checkpoint populations are operational coverage; they are neither late-order recall nor causal evidence of improvement.
Pre-May approved orders and all operational event clocks/queries are bounded before May1; the original final holdout has not been scored or tuned against.
Repeatedly inspected historical/development months cannot become a new untouched test merely by changing the prediction time.
